findings.message: The default launch speed is 5 m/s, but the layout text says the default scrubber range is 0 to 1.020408 s. That range matches a speed of 5 (2·5/9.8), so it is consistent. The problem is that the start frame has height 0 and velocity 5, yet the state label reads 'At launch' while the callout and readout say 'Moving upward'. This is acceptable. The real problem is in the end capture.

At t = 1.020408 s the ball is back at launch height (height 0) with velocity -5. The state label says 'Returned to start' and the motion arrow points down, which is correct. However, the 'v' arrow is 60 px long, the same as at launch. That is consistent. The card still has a scale problem: at launch speed 10 the apex ball is at y=60 and the callout at y=40, close to the lane top at y=34. The ball and the top of its callout sit at the lane edge, and I can't judge clipping without pixels.

The fixed scale is 1.27551 m → 42.5 px, about 33.3 px/m. At launch speed 10, the apex of 5.102 m maps to 170 px, so y=60. The fixed scale is consistent. The scene description says there is no number readout, which holds. At 'rising' (t = 0.2551 s) the v arrow is 30 px long, half of the 60 px at launch. That matches v = 2.5 versus 5.

The motion arrow is absent at the top, as the plan requires. The gravity arrow is 48 px long, pointing down, in every capture. The callout line reads 'At the top' with 'Gravity pulls down'. No contradictions were found. The start-capture finding above is not an error, so the failing verdict rests only on the unverified items. I could not verify the dashed style of the gravity arrow, because the frames give no style data.
